beats.narration_text: Here's the pitch, and I want to be upfront about this part first: nothing in this film has been built yet. It's an honest plan for a tool that checks one thing most agent demos never check.

show.event: types 'I'm building an agent that works.'
corrects 'that works' -> 'that is reliably right, not just right once'

props.text: I'm building an agent that works.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. Pass-at-k: did it succeed at least once across k tries. Pass-caret-k: did it succeed every single time. And a tool contract: the deal a tool makes about what it will actually return.

terms.meaning: succeeded at least once in k tries
what a tool promises to return

qc.sparse_reason: Terms card: three prerequisites, one line each.

beats.narration_text: Picture the thing I'm building as a crate. Open it up, and there's exactly one tool inside — it reaches out and fetches a real page from Python's own documentation.

beats.narration_text: The same source reports the all-three-times number for that same agent at around thirty-four percent — a sixty-three point gap. That gap is the whole reason this tool exists.

beats.narration_text: Here's the other half of the audit: what happens when the tool itself lies to the agent? I'll deliberately feed it a broken response — malformed data, a stale page, a timeout.

shot.visual_intent: One gate on the conveyor cracks and turns jagged; a small warning icon appears over it.

beats.narration_text: From there the crate has two paths. One: it notices and refuses to guess. Two: it quietly passes the bad data through anyway. One of those is safe. The other is the failure mode nobody shows you.

shot.visual_intent: The conveyor forks past the broken gate: one path ends at a stop sign with a check; the other continues through with a faded, uncertain box.
shot.motion_claim: The conveyor forks past the broken gate: one path ends at a stop sign with a check; the other continues through with a faded, uncertain box.

beats.narration_text: I'm keeping this small on purpose: one real tool, ten real questions, one documentation source. The hard part isn't the demo — it's making the interface work with any agent, not just mine. If I run out of time, I'll say so plainly instead of pretending otherwise.

beats.narration_text: Most of this is new to me — I've never built a fault-injection harness before. But the instinct isn't new. In a real pull request I have open right now, I deliberately tried to break a different scoring system and found a real flaw in it. This applies that same habit to agents instead.

beats.narration_text: If you want to try this yourself: paste this into Claude. Pick an agent you've built. Run its hardest task five times in a row. Tell me honestly: did it succeed every single time, or just once? If it has any tool calls, tell me what happens if one of those tools returns something malformed or wrong. Then check two things. Did it actually run five real times, not just once? And did it tell you what happens when a tool lies to it?
